verdict.title: The levels look like they matter
verdict.text: At real levels price bounced 63% of the time it had a clear result, against 50% at control levels (a difference of +12.9 percentage points). That is more than chance would usually produce, so price does seem to react to the real levels.

experiments.name: Trade with the gamma regime
experiments.idea: In negative gamma, only trades in the direction of the last hour's move (dealer hedging amplifies moves). In positive gamma, only trades against it (hedging dampens moves).

experiments.idea: US session only, and new trades only from 9:45 to 11:30 AM New York time, when hedging flow is usually strongest.

experiments.name: Strict rules, US only, checked every minute

experiments.name: Strict rules, US only, checked every 5 minutes
experiments.idea: The same as above but checked every 5 minutes like your scan does now. Comparing the two shows whether checking more often is what helps.

story.title: Gamma regime
story.text: Net gamma is negative. Dealer hedging tends to amplify moves, so swings can run further and faster, and fading a move is riskier. These are overnight levels: the US day's gamma levels with the options that expired at the 4 PM close removed. They are not updated while the options market is closed.

story.title: Where price is
story.text: Nearest level above is the high gamma strike at 25,613, 322 points away. Nearest below is the put wall at 24,786, 504 points away. Price sits between the put wall and the call wall.

story.title: Momentum
story.text: Over the last 30 minutes price moved up 17 points. It is in the bottom third of today's range (24,976 to 26,504).

story.title: Orderflow
story.text: Recent flow shows balanced buying and selling. Price has been falling while buying edges up (bullish divergence). (Estimated from 1 minute bars, not true buy and sell volume.)
